A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VRPO, with matching methods and experiments. All 14 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Tables, equations and figures support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original dialogue, mathematical reasoning and QA experiments, including baseline comparisons, ablations and value-estimation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, component and sensitivity analyses, evaluator validation and results from multiple random seeds.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same VRPO procedure: a variational information bottleneck, entropy/perplexity regularization through a frozen LM head, GAE and PPO updates. External uncertainty scoring and reward-model regularization are evaluated as experimental variants; the proposed core algorithm is unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds SuperGPQA as a scientific training dataset and extends training-time evaluation from four mathematical benchmarks to include SimpleQA, GPQA and HLE. These QA benchmarks already appeared in v1's test-time optimization experiments, but their inclusion in the expanded training-time study substantially broadens that study's coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's PPO and GRPO comparisons, v2 evaluates Reinforce++, Dr.GRPO, KTAE and λ-GRPO in the reasoning experiments (Tables 1, 7 and 12). Dialogue Table 6 also adds a PPO comparator with reward-model improvements, directly testing the value-centric approach against reward-model intervention.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-1.7B evaluations, a human/GPT-4o validation study, and a keyword-attribution protocol using top-20 advantage tokens and specified benchmark samples. Table 6 also changes dialogue checkpoint labels from 250/500/750/1000 to 50/100/150/200 while retaining existing scores; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing that those runs were repeated.

E4.justification: V2 adds an IB-only condition, finer activation sweeps, external-model uncertainty scoring, quantitative keyword attribution, evaluator validation and training-return sensitivity curves. The existing zero-bottleneck experiment is relabelled semantic-only, while the new IB-only condition enables a fuller component comparison. Existing bottleneck-depth and LLaMA studies are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds a four-seed Qwen3-8B VRPO study using seeds 22, 32, 42 and 52 (Table 16), and mentions repeated evaluator sampling. This introduces explicit run-level reporting absent from v1, but remains limited to selected settings; confidence intervals and a formal significance test are not reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for scientific training, new comparators, smaller models, component controls, attribution and evaluator validation. Corresponding train-time entries also change: Qwen3-8B VRPO AIME24 rises from 33.33% in v1 Table 2 to 46.67% in v2 Table 1, and weak-model GRPO AIME24 changes from 0.00% to 6.67%. The original test-time and LLaMA results are retained.

T1.justification: V2 introduces the mathematical definition of Key Token Overlap in Equation 21, using the intersection of high-advantage tokens and reference keywords. The information-bottleneck assumptions and variational derivation remain essentially unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains value-model regularization for robust learning under noisy rewards. V2 strengthens the abstract and concluding account by explicitly claiming denser supervision than reward modeling and correction of reward-induced advantage bias, extending v1's emphasis on absorbing noise and stabilizing PPO.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning component synergy, robustness to activation thresholds, external-scoring checks against self-coupling, and keyword attribution. It also adds specific limitations about test-time-centered ablations, restricted rule-based task coverage, heuristic keyword references and evaluator external validity. These considerably expand v1's interpretation and qualification of the evidence.

D1.justification: V1 leaves unspecified settings as 'set properly.' V2 supplies batch sizes, actor/critic learning rates, generation limits, scientific-data filtering counts, dialogue construction details and a judging rubric with its core prompt. These substantially improve documentation; newly disclosed settings alone do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused positioning against KTAE and λ-GRPO, distinguishing value-model representation learning from explicit token selection or length weighting. It also adds references for SuperGPQA, HLE and contamination concerns. The established reward-robustness and information-bottleneck positioning remains; the updated multivariate-IB publication is the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and experimental narrative are extensively revised. Training-time experiments become the main focus, while test-time results and bottleneck analysis move into expanded appendices. New evaluation subsections, a limitations section and a separate visualization appendix substantially reorganize the document.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document, expands and relocates tables, adds validation and analysis tables, and introduces a sensitivity plot and evaluator-prompt figure. Dialogue plots include the reward-model comparator, noise plots are reorganized, and the existing example heatmaps are redrawn and consolidated onto one appendix page.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited RL comparator set and sparse configuration details, v2 provides more informative controls, component tests and reproducibility information. These strengthen assessment of the value-model claim. However, inconsistent λ-GRPO scores between Tables 7 and 12, unexplained dialogue checkpoint relabelling, and statistical-significance claims without a reported test limit the reliability of the expanded evidence. The net quality gain is positive but qualified.
